investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T10:57–11:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints on the remote agent pod spec. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote agent pod remains in Pending/Unschedulable state until the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected signal and no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in this packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads consuming that extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have had labels removed, taints added, or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity rules may have been tightened, shrinking the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool may not have been scaled to meet concurrent eval demand, especially if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same resource slots.

Lower confidence — a recent change to the pod spec submitted by the remote agent creation path (not visible in the supplied source artifacts) may have added or changed node affinity rules, reducing the eligible node count from a previously larger set to the current 4-node mismatch.

If no other workloads or pods were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, it would suggest the resource limit is set too low in the node configuration rather than being consumed by competing workloads.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking All Remote Agent Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T11:00–11:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both eligible nodes (2/2 nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"). The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~141–148 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the runner to collect any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims available, meaning all VM slots on the two kata-peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads or leaked pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods nodes), so even if VM slots were freed, the cluster has limited capacity headroom for this workload class.

TERTIARY — resource leak or stuck pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previously created eval or user pods did not terminate cleanly, their VM resource allocations may not have been released, exhausting capacity for new pods.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — node affinity/selector misconfiguration in the pod spec: if the selector was recently tightened or the node labels changed, fewer nodes would qualify; however, the message pattern ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') points to capacity exhaustion on the correct nodes rather than a selector mismatch on all nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T10:57–11:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints on the remote agent pod spec. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote agent pod remains in Pending/Unschedulable state until the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected signal and no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in this packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads consuming that extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have had labels removed, taints added, or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity rules may have been tightened, shrinking the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool may not have been scaled to meet concurrent eval demand, especially if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same resource slots.

Lower confidence — a recent change to the pod spec submitted by the remote agent creation path (not visible in the supplied source artifacts) may have added or changed node affinity rules, reducing the eligible node count from a previously larger set to the current 4-node mismatch.
